label: Influenza Returns In October 1920
detail: A renewed wave of influenza sweeps American cities in October 1920, closing public places and keeping many people away from the polls.
assumption: Turnout falls in urban and crowded areas, especially among women, new voters and the poor, while campaign coverage is dominated by the epidemic and health concerns over prices and the treaty.
facts_text: Since early October 1920 a new wave of influenza has spread through American cities, with thousands of cases reported each week.
Health officers in many states have closed schools, theaters and public meeting halls, and have urged people to avoid crowds through election day.

add_planks.text: Expand federal support for public health services and research into epidemic disease.

research_questions: How much did turnout fall in cities hit by the 1918 influenza epidemic in the November 1918 midterm elections?
